unit.title: Cold War and Decolonization
unit.description: Study how the Cold War divided the world, how colonies won independence, how new states and movements challenged established power, and why the Cold War ended.

lesson.title: Global Resistance to Established Power Structures After 1900
lesson.summary: How movements used nonviolence, and sometimes violence, to challenge discrimination and authoritarian rule.
learningGoals: Explain various reactions to existing power structures in the period after 1900.
lesson.bigIdea: People around the world challenged unjust power through nonviolent protest and, in some cases, armed struggle; governments responded with reform or repression.
lesson.context: Gandhi's success in India inspired movements around the world, but not every movement or government chose nonviolence.

sections.title: Nonviolent resistance

blocks.text: In the United States, the civil rights movement used boycotts, marches, and sit-ins to end legal segregation. Martin Luther King Jr. drew on Gandhi's methods, and the movement won the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

In South Africa, the government imposed apartheid, a system of racial segregation, after 1948. The African National Congress protested peacefully until the government banned it in 1960; it then formed an armed wing. International boycotts and protest within South Africa ended apartheid, and Nelson Mandela became president in 1994.

blocks.title: Comparison
blocks.text: King and Mandela both fought racial discrimination, but King's movement stayed nonviolent, while the ANC turned to armed struggle after peaceful protest was banned.

sections.takeaway: Nonviolent movements inspired by Gandhi challenged racial discrimination on several continents.

sections.title: Armed challenges and repression

blocks.text: Some movements used violence. In Peru, the Maoist Shining Path waged a guerrilla war from 1980. Governments also used force against protest: in the Prague Spring of 1968, Czech reformers loosened censorship, and Warsaw Pact armies invaded to end the reforms. In 1989 the Chinese army crushed pro-democracy protests in Tiananmen Square.
In Latin America, military governments such as Augusto Pinochet's in Chile, which seized power in 1973, killed or imprisoned thousands of opponents.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: Not every challenge succeeded. Many protest movements were crushed, and some armed movements caused great suffering of their own.

sections.takeaway: Challenges to power took violent and nonviolent forms, and many governments met them with repression.

connections.title: Gandhi's legacy
connections.body: The nonviolent noncooperation Gandhi led in India between the wars became a model for movements around the world.
connections.transferQuestion: How did Gandhi's methods influence later movements?
connections.feedback: Name a later movement and a method it borrowed.
